sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
I added a groceries row to `budget.csv`:

```
groceries,600,keep under $600; flag anything that would push it over
```

The file only stores limits, so the "flag anything over" part is a note in that row. Nothing in the file will flag overspending by itself. I'll flag it if you share grocery spending or planned purchases with me.

The $600 is the cap, so the budget should stay under it. If you want a hard "under $600" margin, you could set the limit to 599.

cat > meal-plan.md <<'EOF'
# Meal plan: December 2026

Grocery list: see `groceries.csv`.

## Budget
- Planned total: **$594.00**
- Monthly limit (`budget.csv`): $600
- Headroom: **$6.00**. This is under budget, but only just.

## Flags
- Any addition of more than $6 pushes the month over $600. Offset it by cutting something else.
- Biggest categories: fresh vegetables ($70), chicken ($64), fresh fruit ($45).
- Easy places to trim if needed: snacks ($28), coffee and tea ($24), fish ($36).

## Weekly outline
- **Week 1:** Chicken and rice bowls, lentil soup, pasta with tomato sauce, veggie omelets.
- **Week 2:** Beef and bean chili, chicken stir-fry, fish with roasted vegetables, tortilla wraps.
- **Week 3:** Baked chicken thighs, pasta with vegetables, bean and cheese burritos, oatmeal breakfasts.
- **Week 4:** Turkey meatballs, fish tacos, fried rice with eggs, leftover-night soups.

## Notes
- Costs are estimates, so check them against actual receipts.
- Breakfasts are oats, eggs, yogurt and fruit.
- Lunches are mostly leftovers.
EOF

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I wrote `groceries.csv` with 19 items and put the summary in `meal-plan.md`. The planned total is $594.00, which is $6 under your $600 limit.

- **Tight margin:** Adding more than $6 of groceries puts the month over budget. I flagged this in `meal-plan.md`.
- **Where to trim:** The largest items are fresh vegetables ($70), chicken ($64) and fresh fruit ($45). Snacks, coffee and tea, and fish are the easiest to cut.
- **Prices are estimates:** I made up the costs, so check them against your actual receipts.
- **Meal plan:** `meal-plan.md` also has a four-week dinner outline. I titled it "December 2026", since today is Nov 3 and I took "next month" to mean December.
